title: orchestra configuration
description: A project's `.claude/orchestra.json`, read from the primary checkout. Every key is optional.

$schema.description: This schema's address, so an editor completes the file.

stateRoot.description: The folder every programme's state lives under. `~` is the home folder; a relative path is read from the primary checkout. Null is `orchestra` in the platform's folder for a user's application data: %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support on macOS, $XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share elsewhere. Never under a `.claude` folder, whose files an agent cannot write without a prompt.

claude.description: The Claude Code program `orchestra status --measure` runs to read the usage limits, used only where `claude` is not on PATH. `~` is the home folder; a relative path is read from the primary checkout. The desktop app's bundled program lies in a folder named for its version, so a path to it goes stale at each update. Null finds `claude` on PATH alone.

base.description: The branch a session branch is cut from; `orchestra init --base <branch>` names another for one session.

models.description: Model profiles by name; the dispatch hook gives an agent the profile its brief names, `default` otherwise, and none where this holds no `default`.

model.description: The model the agent runs on, as an alias: an Agent call takes no full model id.

effort.description: The agent's effort level; the levels a model offers depend on the model.

contextCeiling.description: The context, in tokens, past which the dispatch hook refuses to resume an agent, since a resume sends the whole context again. The default is the 200K window a session compacts at where a model holds no 1M context.

queues.description: Owners a finding may be routed to besides an agent, beyond the built-in `owner`, `ending` and `handoff`.

preflight.description: Commands `doctor` runs, each of which must exit 0 before a session works.

run.description: The command, its program first, one argument an item.

steps.description: Each runs where the merge touches a path under one of its `when`: installs first, then regenerations, then checks.

when.description: Paths from the root, compared as written, so with no `*`; a path ending in `/` names a folder.

run.description: The command, its program first, one argument an item.

cwd.description: The folder it runs in, from the root.

writes.description: A regeneration's outputs, compared as written, so with no `*`; a conflict in one is answered by running it.

lenses.description: Which of the review's lenses this project's changes make due, beside the paths each lens's own `**Applies.**` line names.

triggers.description: Each makes its lens due where the change touches a path one of its `when` patterns names. A lens whose `**Applies.**` line says `declared` is due only through one, and prints as undeclared where none names it; a public project declares `disclosure` over `**`.

name.description: The lens, as its file is named under the plugin's lenses/ or .claude/orchestra/lenses/, without `.md`.

when.description: Patterns from the root, read as a brief's `Owns:` is: `*` within one folder, `**` any number of folders, a pattern with no `*` itself and every path under it. They add to the paths the lens file names. An empty list makes a `declared` lens due on nothing; a lens whose file says `always` or names paths stays due as the file says.

ci.description: How `ci` waits on a commit's workflow runs, check runs and statuses, and reads the project's own lines in a failed run's log.

workflow.description: The workflow's `name:`, as `gh run list` shows it and not its file name, whose failed log `ci` reads line by line against the expected reds; every other run, check and commit status is read by its conclusion alone.

waitMinutes.description: How long `ci --wait` waits for the commit's runs, checks and statuses to appear and conclude.

verdict.description: A regular expression for the project's own summary line of a failed check, its text in a group named `text`.

relay.description: A regular expression for an annotation that only points at other jobs, whose lines carry the findings.

findings.description: Regular expressions for a test runner's or a checker's line naming one finding, in a group named `text`.

cases.description: Regular expressions for a runner's line naming a failing case, in a group named `name`, whose error follows on the next line.

gate.description: The project's whole check, which `ci gate` runs in the primary checkout; null where the project has none.

run.description: The command, its program first, one argument an item; on Windows a shell script runs as ["bash", "./script.sh"]. Its exit code alone is the verdict: 0 is green.
